컴퓨터.x: I do my homework on the computer.

지우개.x: Could you lend me an eraser?
지우개.e: From 지우다 'to erase' plus -개 'tool': like 덮개 'cover'.

여러분.x: Everyone, that's all for today's class. Good work.
여러분.t: Used to address an audience and never includes the speaker; for 'all of us' say 우리 모두.

부치다.m: to send, to mail (a letter, package); to fry (pancakes)
부치다.ex: 어제 우체국에 가서 고향에 소포를 부쳤어요.
부치다.x: Yesterday I went to the post office and mailed a package home.
부치다.e: Homonym: 전을 부치다 means 'to pan-fry Korean pancakes'.
부치다.t: Don't confuse with 붙이다 'to stick, attach' — same pronunciation [부치다].

꽤.forms: 꽤 + adjective/adverb: 꽤 맛있어요 · 꽤 많이
꽤.ex: 그 식당은 비싸지만 음식이 꽤 맛있어요.
꽤.x: That restaurant is expensive, but the food is pretty good.
꽤.t: 꽤 is weaker than 아주 but stronger than 좀 — like English 'pretty' or 'quite'.

가만히.forms: 가만히 있어요 = Stay still; 가만! = Wait a sec!
가만히.ex: 사진을 찍을 때 가만히 있어 주세요.
가만히.x: Please hold still while I take the photo.

문구점.x: I bought a notebook at the stationery store in front of the school.

수수료.ex: 다른 은행 기계에서 돈을 찾으면 수수료를 내야 해요.
수수료.x: If you withdraw money from another bank's machine, you have to pay a fee.
수수료.e: Literally 'handling fee' — a charge for the work done.

줄넘기.x: The kids are jumping rope on the playground.
줄넘기.e: 줄 (rope) + 넘기 (going over, from 넘다) — literally 'rope-crossing.'
줄넘기.t: Pronounced [줄럼끼] — ㄴ becomes ㄹ after ㄹ, and ㄱ is tensed.

프런트.x: I lost my key card, so I called the front desk.
프런트.t: The standard spelling is 프런트, but 프론트 is very common on signs.

보조금.ex: 정부가 전기차를 사는 사람에게 보조금을 줍니다.
보조금.x: The government gives a subsidy to people who buy electric cars.

구조대.x: The rescue team arrived and saved the people safely.

창의성.ex: 요즘 학교에서는 학생들의 창의성을 키우는 교육이 중요해요.
창의성.x: These days, education that develops students' creativity is important in schools.
창의성.e: Literally 'the quality of creating ideas'; -성 = '-ness, -ity': 가능성, 중요성.
창의성.t: Pronounced [창의썽] or [창이썽]; the -성 suffix is usually tensed to [썽].

갤러리.ex: 인사동에는 작은 갤러리가 많아서 구경하기 좋아요.
갤러리.x: Insadong has lots of small galleries, so it's a nice place to look around.
갤러리.e: From English 'gallery'; also used for golf spectators and phone photo apps.

소프트웨어.x: I installed the software I need on my new computer.

멋쩍다.ex: 인사를 했는데 대답이 없어서 멋쩍게 웃었어요.
멋쩍다.x: I said hello but got no answer, so I gave an awkward smile.
멋쩍다.e: The suffix -쩍다 'seeming' also appears in 미심쩍다 'doubtful'.

구두쇠.x: My uncle is a famous cheapskate in the neighborhood.
구두쇠.e: Not related to 구두 'dress shoes'; the origin is uncertain.

현저히.forms: 현저히 + change verb/adjective: 현저히 줄다, 현저히 낮다
현저히.x: The birth rate is decreasing markedly.

공백.m: blank, empty space; gap, hiatus (in time)
공백.ex: 그 가수는 3년의 공백을 깨고 새 앨범을 냈어요.
공백.x: The singer broke a three-year hiatus and released a new album.
공백.e: Literally 'empty and white,' like a blank page.

덤.m: a little extra thrown in for free, bonus
덤.ex: 사과를 샀더니 할머니가 하나를 덤으로 주셨어요.
덤.x: When I bought apples, the grandma gave me one extra for free.
덤.e: A real market custom: sellers add a little extra to keep customers coming back.
덤.t: Markets give 덤; restaurants call a free extra 서비스.

바느질.x: My grandmother is very good at sewing.
바느질.e: From 바늘 'needle' + -질 'handwork'; the ㄹ drops before ㅈ.

맞선.m: arranged blind date (with marriage in mind)
맞선.x: I went on a marriage-minded blind date set up by my mom's friend.
맞선.e: 맞- 'facing each other' + 선, as in 선을 보다 'to size someone up for marriage.'
맞선.t: Use with 보다: 맞선을 보다. 소개팅 is the casual, no-pressure version.

성경.ex: 저는 매일 아침 성경을 조금씩 읽어요.
성경.x: I read a little of the Bible every morning.

명명하다.ex: 과학자들은 새로 발견한 행성을 그의 이름으로 명명했어요.
명명하다.x: The scientists named the newly discovered planet after him.
명명하다.e: Literally 'order a name' — officially giving something its name.

꾀하다.m: to seek, to pursue, to attempt (change, growth); to plot
꾀하다.ex: 회사는 해외 시장 진출을 통해 성장을 꾀하고 있습니다.
꾀하다.x: The company is seeking growth by expanding into overseas markets.
꾀하다.e: From native 꾀 'wit, trick' — 꾀가 많다 means 'clever, crafty'.
꾀하다.t: Formal, with objects like 변화, 발전, 성장; it can be sinister too: 반란을 꾀하다 'plot a rebellion'.

적막하다.x: After everyone left, the house was silent and still.

등락.x: Stock prices swing so much that investing makes me nervous.
등락.t: Pronounced [등낙] — ㄹ becomes ㄴ after ㅇ.

수술실.ex: 의사들이 환자를 데리고 급하게 수술실로 들어갔어요.
수술실.x: The doctors rushed the patient into the operating room.

내적 동기.forms: 내적 동기가 강하다 · 내적 동기를 부여하다
내적 동기.ex: 내적 동기가 있으면 공부를 오래 계속할 수 있어요.
내적 동기.x: If you have intrinsic motivation, you can keep studying for a long time.
내적 동기.t: Pronounced [내쩍 똥기]; -적 turns nouns into adjectives like '-al'.

역학.ex: 역학 전문가들이 감염 경로를 분석하고 있습니다.
역학.x: Epidemiology experts are analyzing the routes of infection.
역학.t: Homonym warning: 역학 (力學) also means 'mechanics/dynamics' in physics; pronounced [여칵].

자고로.m: from of old, since ancient times
자고로.x: Since olden times, people have said health comes first.
자고로.e: Literally 'from ancient times'; it introduces proverbs and old wisdom.
